newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Many Israel teens identify with Rabin killer - panel.
newsitem.headline: Many Israel teens identify with Rabin killer - panel.

text.p: Many Israeli teenagers -- and even some of their teachers -- identify with the attitudes and actions of Yigal Amir, assassin of former prime minister Yitzhak Rabin, a government panel said on Tuesday.

The Education Ministry investigative panel, appointed after high school girls professed gushing admiration for Amir in a nationally broadcast television interview, noted that most teens "totally rejected the murder and the murderer".
However, "worrisome remarks were heard in the schools, neighbourhoods, and communities", the ministry said in a statement released on Tuesday.

The statement quoted a recent high school graduate as saying that "Rabin brought it upon himself -- I can identify with the the feeling of helplessness held by Yigal Amir, and his anger before the assassination."
Amir, a rightwing religious Jew strongly opposed to Arab-Israeli peace talks, hoped to scuttle the process when he gunned down Rabin following a Tel Aviv peace rally in November, 1995.
He is serving a life sentence for the murder.
After the assassination, teachers at one school in central Israel were observed "walking from class to class explaining why Rabin deserved to die", the statement said.
Panel member Eliezer Marcus said instances of youths identifying with Amir appeared more prevalent among disadvantaged teens.
"Bitterness stemming from economic factors spurs hatred. Hatred can be against the Arabs today, tomorrow it may be directed against the Jews," he told reporters.
